lede: The story of Christmas in Duncanville starts in 1845, when Crawford Trees settled here, and in 1880, when a railway built Duncan Switch, and today it centers on Holiday Lights in the Park at Armstrong Park, where the tree is lit and a drone show follows. Duncanville has 2 events on this page, led by Holiday Lights in the Park on Friday, December 4, 2026.
sections: Crawford Trees and the school on the hill

The Handbook of Texas says the land belonged to the Peters Colony, and settlement began when Crawford Trees arrived from Illinois in 1845 and bought several thousand acres south of Camp Dallas. In 1855 Trees donated land for the Little Bethel Male and Female School, which also served as a church until citizens built the Union Hall House in 1881. By the late 1800s Duncanville had dry goods stores, a pharmacy, a domino parlor and a school, though a fire in 1884 destroyed most of the commercial buildings. The Farmers Gin and the Farmers Bank opened in the early 1900s.
Duncan Switch and a city that chose to incorporate

In 1880 the Chicago, Texas and Mexican Central Railway reached the area and built Duncan Switch, named for a line foreman. Charles P. Nance, the first postmaster, renamed the settlement Duncanville in 1882, and the Gulf, Colorado and Santa Fe took over the railroad in 1883. Fearing annexation by Dallas, residents incorporated a 225 acre city on August 2, 1947. When the population reached 5,000 in 1962, citizens adopted a home rule charter. The Texas Almanac lists 14,105 people in 1970 and 40,706 in 2020.
Holiday Lights in the Park and Cookies with Santa

The City of Duncanville's Holiday Lights in the Park fills Armstrong Park, 100 James Collins Boulevard, on Friday, December 4, 2026, from 5 to 9 pm. Festivities begin at 5 pm, the holiday parade starts at 6:30 pm, the tree is lit at 8:30 pm and a drone show follows at 8:40 pm. The 2025 edition was held on Friday, December 5, with live entertainment, vendors and food. On Saturday, December 12, from 10 am to 1 pm, Cookies with Santa at the Duncanville Recreation Center lets kids meet Santa and decorate cookies, and the city's December series also lists The Polar Express in the Park on December 19.

What is Holiday Lights in the Park in Duncanville?

Holiday Lights in the Park is the City of Duncanville's tree lighting festival at Armstrong Park, 100 James Collins Blvd. In 2026 it is Friday, December 4, from 5 to 9 pm, with a parade at 6:30 pm, the tree lighting at 8:30 pm and a drone show at 8:40 pm. The city's Instagram post calls it free.
Is Cookies with Santa free in Duncanville?

Yes. Duncanville Parks and Recreation calls Cookies with Santa a free event in its own Instagram post. It is Saturday, December 12, 2026, from 10 am to 1 pm at the Duncanville Recreation Center, 201 James Collins Blvd, where kids can meet Santa, take pictures and decorate cookies.
